summary: 观看运动时，观众脑中与动作相关的活动可能让他们在一定程度上体验运动员的表现。文章由镜像神经元实验讲到观察学习，最后用这一机制解释观赛的吸引力。
logic: 从观看竞技的历史发问
解释所见动作与自身运动的对应

paragraphs.brief: 在诗人霍默发明史诗的同时古希腊人开始了一个节日男人们在一场200米长的比赛中竞争
sentences: At about the same time that the poet Homer invented the epic there, the ancient Greeks started a festival in which men competed in a single race, about 200 metres long.
在诗人霍默发明史诗的同时古希腊人开始了一个节日男人们在一场200米长的比赛中竞争
The winner received a branch of wild olives.
赢家收到了一枝野生橄榄
The Greeks called this celebration the Olympics.
希腊人称此为奥运会庆典
Though the ancient sprint remains, today the Olympics are far more than that.
虽然古代的短跑仍然存在，但今天的奥运远不止如此。
Indeed, the Games seem to celebrate the dream of progress as embodied in the human form.
事实上，奥运会似乎庆祝人类形式的进步梦想。
That the Games are intoxicating to watch is beyond question.
游戏令人兴奋观看是不容置疑的。
During the Athens Olympics in 2004, 3.4 billion people, half the world, watched them on television.
在2004年雅典奥运会期间，34亿人在电视上观看，他们占世界一半。
Certainly, being a spectator is a thrilling experience—but why?
当然，当观众是令人兴奋的经历，但为什么呢？

paragraphs.brief: 1996年，意大利三名神经科学家Giacomo Rizzolatti、Leonardo Fogassi和Vittorio Gallese检查了猴子的运动前皮层。
sentences: In 1996, three Italian neuroscientists, Giacomo Rizzolatti, Leonardo Fogassi and Vittorio Gallese, examined the premotor cortex of monkeys.
1996年，意大利三名神经科学家Giacomo Rizzolatti、Leonardo Fogassi和Vittorio Gallese检查了猴子的运动前皮层。
They discovered that inside these primate brains there were groups of cells that ‘store vocabularies of motor actions’, just as there are grammars of movement.
他们发现在这些灵长类大脑里，有一群细胞“运动动作的词层”，就像有运动语法一样。
These networks of cells are the bodily ‘sentences’ we use every day, the ones our brain has chosen to retain and refine.
这些细胞网络是我们每天使用的身体“判决”，我们的大脑选择保留和完善。
Think, for example, about a golf swing.
比如说，打高尔夫球
To those who have only watched the Masters Tournament on TV, golfing seems easy.
那些只看电视主赛的人高尔夫球似乎很容易
To the novice, however, the skill of casting a smooth arc with a lopsided metal stick is virtually impossible.
但是，对于新手来说，用斜面金属棒铸出光滑弧的技巧几乎是不可能的。
This is because most novices swing with their consciousness, using an area of the brain next to the premotor cortex.
这是因为大多数新手都带着意识挥舞着使用大脑在前脑皮层旁边的一个区域
To the expert, on the other hand, a perfectly balanced stroke is second nature.
另一方面，对专家来说，完全平衡的中风是第二种性质。
For him, the motor action has become memorized, and the movements are embedded in the neurons of his premotor cortex.
对他来说，运动动作已经被记住了运动也植入到他前脑皮层的神经元里
He hits the ball with the tranquility of his perfected autopilot.
他用他完美的自动驾驶员的宁静击球

paragraphs.brief: 这些神经元在运动前皮层中，除了解释为什么某些运动员似乎拥有几乎令人难以置信的技能水平，更惊人的特征，促使里佐拉蒂，福加西和加卢斯给他们崇高的称号“神灵神经元”。
sentences: These neurons in the premotor cortex, besides explaining why certain athletes seem to possess almost unbelievable levels of skill, have an even more amazing characteristic, one that caused Rizzolatti, Fogassi and Gallese to give them the lofty title ‘mirror neurons’.
这些神经元在运动前皮层中，除了解释为什么某些运动员似乎拥有几乎令人难以置信的技能水平，更惊人的特征，促使里佐拉蒂，福加西和加卢斯给他们崇高的称号“神灵神经元”。

They note that ‘the main functional characteristic of mirror neurons is that they become active both when the monkey performs a particular action (for example, grasping an object or holding it) and, astonishingly, when it sees another individual performing a similar action’.
他们指出，“镜像神经元的主要功能特征是，当猴子执行某种特定动作(例如，抓住物体或持有物体)时，和当它看到另一个人进行类似动作时，它们都变得活跃。
Humans have an even more elaborate mirror neuron system.
人类有更精密的镜像神经系统
These peculiar cells mirror, inside the brain, the outside world: they enable us to internalize the actions of another.
这些奇特的细胞在大脑里，在外表世界里使我们能够把另一个人的动作内部化。
In order to be activated, though, these cells require what the scientists call ‘goal-orientated movements’.
为了被激活，这些细胞需要科学家所说的“定向运动”。
If we are staring at a photograph, a fixed image of a runner mid-stride, our mirror neurons are totally silent.
如果我们盯着照片看，固定的图像一个跑步中，我们的镜像神经元完全沉默。
They only fire when the runner is active: running, moving or sprinting.
他们只在跑步者活动时开火：跑步、移动或冲刺。

paragraphs.brief: 这些电子生理学研究显示当我们看高尔夫球员或跑步者在行动时镜中神经元在我们自己的运动前皮层灯光中仿佛我们是竞争对手
sentences: What these electrophysiological studies indicate is that when we watch a golfer or a runner in action, the mirror neurons in our own premotor cortex light up as if we were the ones competing.
这些电子生理学研究显示当我们看高尔夫球员或跑步者在行动时镜中神经元在我们自己的运动前皮层灯光中仿佛我们是竞争对手
This phenomenon of neural mirroring was first discovered in 1954, when two French physiologists, Gastaut and Bert, found that the brains of humans vibrate with two distinct wavelengths, alpha and mu.
这种神经镜像现象是1954年首次发现的，当时两名法国物理学家Gastaut和Bert发现，人类的大脑以两种不同的波长，即阿尔法和穆尔振动。
The mu system is involved in neural mirroring.
肌肉系统与神经镜像有关
It is active when our bodies are still, and disappears whenever we do something active, like playing a sport or changing the TV channel.
当我们的身体还在时，它就很活跃，每当我们做一些积极的事情时，它就会消失，比如玩运动或者改变电视频道。
The surprising fact is that the mu signal is also quiet when we watch someone else being active, as on TV.
令人惊讶的是，当我们看到其他人像电视一样活跃时，Mu 信号也是安静的。
These results are the effect of mirror neurons.
这些结果就是镜像神经元的影响。

paragraphs.brief: Rizzolatti、Fogassi和Gallese将镜像神经元称为“直接匹配假设”。
sentences: Rizzolatti, Fogassi and Gallese call the idea of mirror neurons the ‘direct matching hypothesis’.
Rizzolatti、Fogassi和Gallese将镜像神经元称为“直接匹配假设”。
They believe that we only understand the movement of sports stars when we ‘map the visual representation of the observed action onto our motor representation of the same action’.
他们相信我们只有在“将观察到的动作的视觉表现映射到我们运动中的动作”时才会理解体育明星的动作。
According to this theory, watching an Olympic athlete ‘causes the motor system of the observer to resonate.
根据这个理论，看奥运运动员，是因为观察者的运动系统引起共鸣。
The ‘motor knowledge’ of the observer is used to understand the observed action.’
观察员的 " 运动知识 " 被用来理解观察的行动。
But mirror neurons are more than just the neural basis for our attitude to sport.
但是镜像神经元不仅仅是我们对运动的态度的神经基础。
It turns out that watching a great golfer makes us better golfers, and watching a great sprinter actually makes us run faster.
看着一个伟大的高尔夫球手使我们更能打高尔夫并且看一个伟大的跑步运动员确实能让我们跑得更快
This ability to learn by watching is a crucial skill.
这种通过观察学习的能力是一项关键技能。
From the acquisition of language as infants to learning facial expressions, mimesis (copying) is an essential part of being conscious.
从获得作为婴儿的语言到学习面部表情，模仿(复印)是意识的基本组成部分。
The best athletes are those with a premotor cortex capable of imagining the movements of victory, together with the physical properties to make those movements real.
最好的运动员是那些拥有能想象胜利运动的运动前皮层的人还有这些运动的物理特性

paragraphs.brief: 相反，我们看体育感觉，人类戏剧。
sentences: But how many of us regularly watch sports in order to be a better athlete?
我们有多少人定期看体育比赛才能成为更好的运动员？
Rather, we watch sport for the feeling, the human drama.
相反，我们看体育感觉，人类戏剧。
This feeling also derives from mirror neurons.
这种感觉也来自镜像神经元。
By letting spectators share in the motions of victory, they also allow us to share in its feelings.
让观众分享胜利运动，也让我们分享其感受。
This is because they are directly connected to the amygdala, one of the main brain regions involved in emotion.
这是因为他们直接与阿米格达拉相连，这是情感中主要的大脑区域之一。
During the Olympics, the mirror neurons of whole nations will be electrically identical, their athletes causing spectators to feel, just for a second or two, the same thing.
在奥运期间，整个国家的镜像神经元将完全相同，他们的运动员使观众感到，只是一秒钟或两秒，同样的事情。
Watching sports brings people together.
观看体育使人们聚集在一起。
Most of us will never run a mile in under four minutes, or hit a home run.
我们大多数人不会在四分钟内跑一英里也不会打全垒打
Our consolation comes in watching.
我们的安慰是看着的。
When we gather around the TV, we all feel, just for a moment, what it is to do something perfectly.
当我们聚集在电视周围，我们都感觉，只是一瞬间，什么是做一些完美的事情。

items.en: an explanation of why watching sport may be emotionally satisfying
items.zh: 解释为什么看体育可能是情感满足
items.why: F 段把镜像神经元和负责情绪的杏仁核联系起来，解释了观众为何能借运动员完成动作获得情感体验。

items.en: an explanation of why beginners find sporting tasks difficult
items.zh: 解释初学者为何难于完成运动任务
items.why: B 段说新手常有意识地控制每次挥动，需要动用与熟练动作不同的处理方式，由此解释初学者为何觉得这些动作困难。

items.en: a factor that needs to combine with mirroring to attain sporting excellence
items.zh: 需要与镜像相结合，才能取得优异的体育成绩
items.why: E 段说顶尖运动员要同时具备预演成功动作的脑机制和真正做出动作的身体条件，点出镜像能力还需什么配合。

items.en: a comparison of human and animal mirror neurons
items.zh: 人与动物镜神经元的比较
items.why: C 段拿动物与人的镜像系统作比较，指出人的系统更加复杂，再讨论它在观察动作时怎样参与反应。

items.en: the first discovery of brain activity related to mirror neurons
items.zh: 首次发现与镜像神经元有关的大脑活动
items.why: D 段把最早的相关发现追溯至 1954 年两位法国生理学家的脑电研究，并介绍他们辨认出的两种脑电波。

items.en: a claim linking observation to improvement in performance
items.zh: 一项将观察与业绩改善联系起来的索赔
items.why: E 段明确提出，观看优秀高尔夫球手或短跑运动员表演，有助于改善观看者相应的运动表现。

items.en: The writer uses the term ‘grammar of movement’ to mean
items.zh: 作者使用 " 运动语法 " 一词表示：

items.en: The writer states that expert players perform their actions
items.zh: 作者说，专业的玩家他们的行动

items.en: The writer states that the most common motive for watching sport is to
items.zh: 作家说看体育最常用的动机是

items.en: Inexpert sports players are too aware of what they are doing.
items.zh: 专业体育运动员非常清楚他们在做什么。
items.why: too aware 与“用意识在挥杆"同义，说明注意力过强、未自动化，故 YES。

items.en: Monkeys have a more complex mirror neuron system than humans.
items.zh: 猴子的镜像神经系统比人类复杂
items.why: 文意与题干相反 (人类比猴子更复杂),故 NO。

items.en: Looking at a photograph can activate mirror neurons.
items.zh: 看着照片就能激活镜像神经元
items.why: 了明确说“照片不激活",与题干相反，故 NO。

items.en: Gastaut and Bert were both researchers and sports players.
items.zh: Gastaut和Bert都是研究人员和运动员。
items.why: 加斯托和贝尔被介绍为研究脑电波的法国生理学家。文中没有介绍两人的运动经历，无法确定他们是否也是运动员。

items.en: The mu system is at rest when we are engaged in an activity.
items.zh: 当我们从事一项活动时，穆尔系统处于休息状态。
items.why: 题干“at rest (静息/安静) "与文中“disappears/quiet” 同义。我们在进行活动时 py 不活跃，故 YES。

pairs: 不经有意识的思考／自动进行
不经思考就能完成／变成了本能

clauses: At about the same time that the poet Homer invented the epic there, the ancient Greeks started a festival ….

读到 which 时，回看 festival，再把修饰信息接回主句。

连接词 if 引出“If we are staring at a photograph, a fixed image of a runner mid-stride”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
